source_pages_visually_inspected.observation: Exact source page 1 actually viewed: title, Espen R. Jakobsen and Artur Rutkowski and arXiv:2305.18867v2 [math.AP] 24 Jan 2025 are visible. Appendix A-D contents and 61-page binding match the stored review.

Exact source p.6 actually viewed: the C_b^k norm is explicitly the sum of sup norms of derivatives, and the dual-space definition follows. This confirms the primal norm used by P4 rather than assuming an equivalent but different product norm.

Exact source page 7 actually viewed: Lemma 2.3 quantifies every delta>0 and its proof prints C epsilon^delta, confirming P7's target. Definition 2.5 explicitly introduces measure-representability and nonuniqueness of representation; the Banach-limit distinction supporting rejection of the invalid counterexample is visible.

Exact source p.8 actually viewed: Lemma 2.6 prints the exact dual norm as a sum of total variations; Lemma 2.7 reuses it. The measure-representable restriction and subsequent mixed Holder spaces are visible, matching P4's precise norm correction and limited downstream impact.

Exact source p.14 actually viewed: (K) first quantifies one K>0 and alpha in (1,2], then all beta in N^d with the same K in the L1 derivative estimate. This confirms the literal quantifier targeted by P3; Remark 2.22 and F1/F2 are legible.

Exact source p.16 actually viewed: (M3) is value-independent and (M4) permits H1(x,p)+H2(x,u) with 0<=D_u H2<=c2. The operator examples explicitly list L=Delta and alpha=2, with a Gaussian footnote. This confirms the intended-operator qualification in P1/P6 and the literal-scope issue P3.

Exact source p.20 actually viewed: the forward equation has +H=0 while the printed mild integral has +H, confirming P7's sign target. The distinction between standard monotonicity and the stronger dual-space positivity (2.12) is explicitly discussed and matches retained scope.

Exact source p.21 actually viewed: Lemma 3.3(b) explicitly gives a common modulus independent of f and z0 for the time derivative as well as the weaker spatial norm. The hypotheses and (3.2) are legible, confirming P6's uniformity target.

Exact source p.23 actually viewed: Lemma 3.5 assumes V1 continuous bounded, V2 bounded in time with L1 spatial norm, and rho0 in L1; positivity or a probability normalization is not assumed. Equation (3.9) and the preceding distinction between spatial and time derivatives are legible, confirming the existing P1/P6 hypothesis boundaries.

Exact source p.24 actually viewed: signed equation (3.10) has an additive divergence V2; Lemma 3.5(e) prints a weighted absolute moment with only initial weighted mass, unweighted L1 source/solution norms and fixed tightness-function coefficients. This matches P1 without silently replacing the signed equation by a probability equation.

Exact source p.25 actually viewed: the proof integrates (t-s)^(-2/alpha) and then writes an epsilon^(1-2/alpha) bound, including the alpha=2 endpoint. The printed estimate and ensuing (3.18) match P6's logarithmic correction.

Exact source p.26 actually viewed: Lemma 3.5(e)'s proof says to test with psi and cites [34, Proposition 6.6(c)]. Immediately following Theorem 3.6 is explicitly a probability-density, source-free equation. The source's citation and the distinction relevant to P1 are legible; [34]'s full proof remains an unverified external dependency.
Exact source p.29 actually viewed: (3.27) asserts a forcing-independent time modulus; the fixed-point formula and (3.28) use H-f. These are the exact printed expressions addressed in P6/P7.

Exact source p.31 actually viewed: the value-dependent H1+H2 split, definitions of I(s), J(s), and final A(s)+c2 integral_s^T A >= J(s) inequality are legible. They match the scalar inference isolated in P2, without asserting an MFG nonuniqueness example.

Exact source p.32 actually viewed: the first display concludes C A(t0)>=J(t0) 'By Gronwall'; Theorem 4.3(b) and its use of Lemma 4.2 are visible. This confirms P2's proof-gap target and its value-dependent scope.

Exact source p.37 actually viewed: Theorem 5.5 Step 2 expressly cites Lemma 3.5(b),(c),(e) for boundedness, translation continuity and tightness, establishing the reported P1 compactness dependency. The energy identities (5.15)-(5.17) remain separate.

Exact source p.41 actually viewed: the passage from arbitrary delta loss to (5.27), the beta integral and measure-representability argument are legible. The report correctly leaves uniformity of this passage as a limitation rather than asserting a counterexample to the smoothing theorem.

Exact source p.42 actually viewed: Corollary 5.8 uses t^(gamma/alpha) although t ranges from t0; Lemma 5.9 displays dependence on y1-y2 alone. The formulas targeted by P5/P7 and their stated parameters are visible.

Exact source p.44 actually viewed: Lemma 5.9 is invoked for coefficients evaluated at solution gradients; Theorems 4.3,5.3,5.5 provide prior uniform solution bounds. Corollary 5.8 is used for an integrable time singularity. These support the report's limited impact/repair boundaries.

Exact source p.46 actually viewed: the superlinear Taylor-remainder step explicitly invokes Lemma 5.9. Definition 6.1 and Theorem 6.2's hypothesis list, including (K) and (M1)-(M3), are visible; the report does not turn a local proof defect into a nonuniqueness claim.

Exact source p.50 actually viewed: the end of the master-equation uniqueness construction uses the value-independent MFG system. Appendix A begins with the jet-product/Hahn-Banach representation argument, matching P4's location and the report's separation of value-dependent uniqueness.

Exact source p.51 actually viewed: (A.2) prints a sum-total-variation norm, and after (A.6) equality of individual lift norms is used to infer the chosen lifts are Cauchy. The exact P4 target is visible; the corrected closure argument remains as previously supplied. Appendix B starts below.

Exact source p.52 actually viewed: Lemma B.2 states a weaker spatial Holder-norm time modulus and begins its Duhamel proof. It does not assert the forcing-independent time-derivative modulus targeted in P6. This preserves the report's explicit counterevidence and downstream limitation.
